sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.body: Security on Civis is not a feature — it is the foundational architecture. Sovereign governments entrust the platform with the personal data of their citizens abroad, and that trust requires a zero-trust, audit-first, government-grade security posture embedded into every layer from the first line of code.

sections.title: Zero-Trust Architecture
sections.body: No implicit trust exists at any layer. Every request — regardless of origin — is verified, authenticated, and authorized before processing. Internal service calls are authenticated, database queries are gated by Row-Level Security, and storage access requires signed URLs.

sections.title: Sovereign Cloud and On-Premise Deployment
sections.body: Civis Cloud operates on hardened shared infrastructure with regional selection. Civis Government provides a dedicated environment in a government-specified hosting region. Civis Sovereign delivers fully dedicated infrastructure provisioned through infrastructure-as-code — open to government inspection and independent audit.

sections.title: Encryption Standards
sections.body: All data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. All data in transit uses TLS 1.3 (TLS 1.2 minimum) with HSTS enforced on every platform domain. Highly sensitive fields — identity document references and economic profiles — receive additional field-level access gating.

sections.title: Row-Level Security and Tenant Isolation
sections.body: Tenant isolation is enforced at three independent layers — middleware, service layer, and database RLS policies. Cross-tenant access is technically impossible: one government's data can never be accessed by another, and every attempt is logged as a security event.

sections.title: Immutable Audit Trail Architecture
sections.body: Every sensitive action generates an immutable audit record before a success response is returned. Audit logs permit no update or deletion, are retained for a minimum of seven years, and are exportable in CSV and PDF for regulatory review.

sections.title: Identity and Access Management
sections.body: Eight platform roles operate under least-privilege access. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all administrative roles, passwords require a twelve-character minimum with complexity enforcement, and sessions use short-lived tokens with refresh rotation.

sections.title: Compliance Framework
sections.body: ISO 27001-aligned security management, SOC 2 Type II architecture across all five trust service criteria, GDPR and NDPR compliance, and AU Malabo Convention alignment — with controls evidence available to sovereign clients under NDA.

sections.title: Penetration Testing and Vulnerability Management
sections.body: Annual full-scope third-party penetration testing, quarterly RLS policy verification, and automated dependency scanning on every change. Critical findings carry a 24-hour remediation SLA. Sovereign clients may commission independent testing of their dedicated infrastructure.

sections.title: Incident Response Overview
sections.body: A structured response playbook with severity classification: containment within hours, sovereign client notification within 72 hours of a confirmed breach — 4 hours for critical incidents — regulatory notification per GDPR Article 33, and a full post-incident review within 30 days.

whitepaper.ctaTitle: Request the Full Security Architecture Document
whitepaper.ctaBody: The complete Security Architecture Specification — threat model, controls evidence, and SOC 2 mapping — is available to government procurement teams under NDA.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: All protected endpoints require a valid JWT access token issued through the platform authentication flow, presented in the Authorization header. The token is validated before any data operation proceeds, and tenant scope is derived server-side — never trusted from the client.

versioning.body: All routes use URL path versioning. Breaking changes require a new major version, with the previous version supported for a minimum of twelve months. Government and Sovereign tier clients receive advance notification of all breaking changes.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Afronovation, Inc. operates Civis, the sovereign diaspora intelligence platform. This policy describes how personal data is collected, used, and protected across the platform. Privacy on Civis is a sovereign trust obligation — earned through architecture, not asserted through policy documents alone.

sections.title: Data We Collect
sections.body: The platform processes the following categories of data, each under a defined classification level:
items: Identity data — name, date of birth, nationality
Contact data — email address, phone number, country and city of residence
Authentication data — account credentials and session records
Registry data — professional background, household information, and voluntary economic profile data
Technical data — IP address, browser type, and device information captured for security and audit purposes

sections.title: How We Use Your Data
sections.body: Personal data is processed only for the purposes stated at the time of collection:
items: Service delivery — operating the registry, embassy workspace, and registrant portal
Authentication and account security
Audit and regulatory compliance — immutable records of sensitive actions
Aggregated, anonymized analytics — never individual-level surveillance

sections.title: Data Sovereignty and Storage
sections.body: Every government tenant is cryptographically isolated. Data resides on sovereign or regionally compliant infrastructure, no cross-tenant access is technically possible, and all data is protected with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit.

sections.title: Consent Architecture
sections.body: Informed consent is captured before any personal data is stored. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous — pre-ticked boxes are not permitted. Consent records are immutable, stored with the exact text shown at the time of consent, and withdrawal is supported at any time without adverse consequence.

sections.title: Data Retention
sections.body: Retention periods are configurable per government entity within regulatory minimums. Upon contract termination, personal data is securely erased within 90 days with cryptographic proof of deletion. Audit records are anonymized rather than deleted, as required for regulatory compliance.

sections.title: Your Rights
sections.body: Subject to the configuration of your government entity and applicable law, you may exercise the following rights, with responses within 30 calendar days:
items: Access — obtain a copy of all personal data held about you
Rectification — correct inaccurate or incomplete data
Erasure — request deletion of your personal data
Portability — receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format
Objection — object to processing for specific purposes

sections.title: Applicable Law
sections.body: This policy operates under the GDPR (EU) 2016/679, the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation 2019, the African Union Malabo Convention, and the applicable national data protection legislation of each deploying government.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: Privacy inquiries: privacy@civisos.com. Data Protection Officer: dpo@civisos.com.

sections.title: Acceptance
sections.body: The Civis service is provided exclusively for authorized government entities, diplomatic missions, and their designated personnel. Use of the platform constitutes acceptance of these terms by the government entity and its authorized users.

sections.title: Service Description
sections.body: Civis is a sovereign intelligence platform comprising a diaspora registry, embassy workspace, sovereign analytics, and the Dia AI intelligence engine, delivered across three deployment tiers: Civis Cloud, Civis Government, and Civis Sovereign.

sections.title: Government Entity Obligations
sections.body: Each government entity agrees to:
items: Designate a platform administrator responsible for tenant governance
Ensure personnel comply with applicable security clearance requirements
Maintain the confidentiality of access credentials
Report suspected security incidents without delay

sections.title: Intellectual Property
sections.body: All platform intellectual property is owned by Afronovation, Inc. Government entities retain full and exclusive ownership of all data they enter into the platform — no rights to government data are transferred to Afronovation under any circumstance.

sections.title: Service Level Agreement
sections.body: Afronovation commits to 99.9% monthly uptime. Scheduled maintenance is announced with 72 hours' notice; emergency security patches may be deployed without advance notice where required to protect sovereign data.

sections.title: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: Liability is limited in accordance with standard commercial terms for government software services, capped at the total fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim.

sections.title: Termination
sections.body: Either party may terminate with 90 days' written notice. Upon termination, the government entity receives a 30-day data export window, followed by secure deletion of all tenant data with cryptographic proof.

sections.title: Scope and Purpose
sections.body: This Data Processing Agreement governs the relationship between Afronovation, Inc. as data processor and the deploying government entity as data controller, in compliance with the GDPR, the AU Malabo Convention, and the NDPR.

sections.title: Processing Instructions
sections.body: The processor acts only on documented instructions from the controller. If an instruction would violate applicable data protection law, the processor notifies the controller immediately before any processing occurs.

sections.title: Technical Security Measures
sections.body: The processor implements and maintains the following technical measures:
items: AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit
Row-Level Security enforcing tenant isolation at the database layer
Multi-factor authentication for all administrative access
Immutable audit logging of all data access and modification events
Regular third-party penetration testing and vulnerability assessments
Incident response with 72-hour notification to the controller

sections.title: Sub-processors
sections.body: Approved sub-processors and their processing scope are disclosed to the controller: Supabase (database and storage), Vercel (application hosting and delivery), and the hosting providers applicable to the selected deployment tier. Sub-processors are security-assessed before deployment and annually thereafter.

sections.title: Data Subject Rights
sections.body: The processor supports the controller in fulfilling all data subject rights requests — access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, and portability — within 30 days.

sections.title: Cross-Border Transfers
sections.body: Data is transferred across borders only with appropriate safeguards: Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy decisions, or deployment on sovereign infrastructure that eliminates the transfer entirely.

sections.title: Termination
sections.body: Upon termination of services, all personal data is securely deleted within 90 days with cryptographic proof of deletion, subject to legal hold obligations.

sections.title: What Cookies We Use
sections.body: The Civis public platform uses essential cookies only:
items: Session security cookies protecting authentication state
Locale preference (NEXT_LOCALE) — remembers your EN/FR language selection
Cookie consent record (civis_cookie_consent) — stores your consent choice

sections.title: What We Do Not Use
sections.body: No advertising cookies. No third-party tracking. No analytics cookies are set without explicit consent.

sections.title: Cookie Consent
sections.body: A consent banner is presented at the bottom of the screen on first load. Your choice is stored in the civis_cookie_consent cookie for 365 days. Consent may be withdrawn at any time by clearing your browser cookies.

sections.title: Third-Party Cookies
sections.body: The public marketing platform sets no third-party cookies. The authenticated platform may use Mapbox (map tile delivery) and Supabase (authentication session) cookies, both covered by sub-processor agreements.

sections.title: Managing Cookies
sections.body: Cookies can be reviewed and removed through your browser settings. Blocking essential cookies may prevent core platform functionality, including language preference and secure sign-in.
